findings.title: Missing @nonreentrant on withdraw()
findings.description: Function ``withdraw()`` is @external, performs an external call or value transfer, but does not use the @nonreentrant decorator. This exposes the contract to reentrancy attacks.
findings.why_flagged: Function ``withdraw()`` is @external, performs an external call or value transfer, but does not use the @nonreentrant decorator. This exposes the contract to reentrancy attacks.

findings.title: Missing @nonreentrant on deposit()
findings.description: Function ``deposit()`` is @external and modifies state without the @nonreentrant decorator. This can be exploited via cross-function reentrancy if another function in the contract makes external calls.
findings.why_flagged: Function ``deposit()`` is @external and modifies state without the @nonreentrant decorator. This can be exploited via cross-function reentrancy if another function in the contract makes external calls.

findings.title: Unchecked raw_call in execute()
findings.description: ``raw_call()`` in ``execute()`` does not have its return value asserted. If the external call fails silently, state may become inconsistent.
findings.fix_suggestion: Wrap the call: ``assert raw_call(...)``, or capture the success flag and assert it.
findings.why_flagged: ``raw_call()`` in ``execute()`` does not have its return value asserted. If the external call fails silently, state may become inconsistent.

findings.title: No event emitted in withdraw()
findings.description: Function ``withdraw()`` modifies contract state but does not emit an event (``log``).  Events are essential for off-chain indexers and transparency.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add a ``log`` statement at the end of ``withdraw()``.
findings.why_flagged: Function ``withdraw()`` modifies contract state but does not emit an event (``log``).  Events are essential for off-chain indexers and transparency.

findings.title: Unprotected selfdestruct in destroy()
findings.description: ``selfdestruct()`` in ``destroy()`` can be called by anyone — no ``msg.sender`` check was found. An attacker can destroy the contract.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add ``assert msg.sender == self.owner`` (or equivalent) before the ``selfdestruct()`` call.
findings.why_flagged: ``selfdestruct()`` in ``destroy()`` can be called by anyone — no ``msg.sender`` check was found. An attacker can destroy the contract.

findings.title: Unprotected write to self.total_deposited in deposit()
findings.description: ``deposit()`` writes to ``self.total_deposited`` without checking ``msg.sender``. Anyone can call this function and change a sensitive state variable.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add ``assert msg.sender == self.owner`` (or equivalent) at the top of ``deposit()``.
findings.why_flagged: ``deposit()`` writes to ``self.total_deposited`` without checking ``msg.sender``. Anyone can call this function and change a sensitive state variable.

findings.fix_suggestion: Add ``assert msg.sender == self.owner`` (or equivalent) at the top of ``set_owner()``.
findings.why_flagged: ``set_owner()`` writes to ``self.owner`` without checking ``msg.sender``. Anyone can call this function and change a sensitive state variable.

findings.title: CEI violation in withdraw()
findings.description: ``withdraw()`` performs an external call (``send``) **before** updating state on a reachable execution path. Callback feasibility is ``attacker_controlled``; target trust is ``caller_controlled``; state dependencies are ``balances``. Move all state changes above the external call (Checks → Effects → Interactions).
findings.fix_suggestion: Reorder the function: perform all state updates (self.x = …) BEFORE any external calls (send / raw_call / interface calls). This is the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
findings.why_flagged: A reachable path performs an external call before state mutation.
findings.why_not_suppressed: The call and later state write occur on the same reachable path.

exploit_verification.why_exploitable: The function performs an external interaction before committing state. If the callee can re-enter this entrypoint or another state-dependent entrypoint, it may observe stale accounting.

patch.summary: Move state writes before the external call and keep/ add @nonreentrant.

regression_test.name: test_withdraw_cei_reentrancy_path
plan: deploy vulnerable contract and attacker callback contract
fund the victim state needed by withdraw()
call withdraw() from the attacker contract
assert the attacker cannot withdraw/receive more than its committed balance after the patch

findings.title: Missing zero-address check for self.owner in set_owner()
findings.description: ``set_owner()`` sets ``self.owner`` (an address) from ``new_owner`` without verifying it is non-zero. Setting it to ``empty(address)`` can permanently lose critical functionality (ownership, fee recipient, etc.).
findings.fix_suggestion: Add ``assert new_owner != empty(address)`` before assigning to ``self.owner``.
findings.why_flagged: ``set_owner()`` sets ``self.owner`` (an address) from ``new_owner`` without verifying it is non-zero. Setting it to ``empty(address)`` can permanently lose critical functionality (ownership, fee recipient, etc.).
